milestone: Horizen Pilot — recover a registration whose identifier was never persisted
problem: `checkAgentRegistrationStatus` refuses to call Horizen's `get_onboarding_status` without an agentId. For a registration whose `horizenAgentId` was never persisted, the only recovery path in place was a wallet-keyed registry lookup — `fetchRegistryAgent(ownerWalletAddress, network)` — which is a different tool contract than an agentId lookup with no guarantee the two coincide.
observedFailure: The status check reported STATUS_UNAVAILABLE ('the registration's agent identifier was unavailable') for a registration that had genuinely succeeded on chain.

After the identifier was recovered, the check moved to a SECOND failure: MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS — 'Horizen has not confirmed this registration after 20 checks' — because `confirmed` is a substring match over Horizen's flattened prose (active / confirmed / complete) and an answer phrased any other way reports not-confirmed forever.
REGISTRY_REREAD_FAILED refused whenever Horizen's registry reread failed, discarding chain evidence that had already verified the mint because a convenience lookup failed.
rootCauses: An identifier was being recovered through a lookup keyed on a DIFFERENT reference (the owner wallet) than the one being recovered (the agent id). ERC-721 `balanceOf` returns a count, not a list — there is no reverse enumeration guarantee.
A single vendor status string was treated as the only source of truth for a fact the chain itself records.
resolution: `services/horizen/agentIdRecovery.ts` decodes the minted agentId from the registration transaction's own receipt logs — deterministic, read-only, no registry lookup.

Scoped to the repo's own recorded identityRegistry address, refusing on ambiguity (more than one decoded agentId) rather than guessing, and verifying `ownerOf()` against the expected owner before the identifier is ever trusted.

Made the chain a SECOND, independent confirmation source with the source NAMED (`confirmationSource: horizen-status | on-chain-receipt | both`) and any divergence stated in both directions rather than resolved by preferring one.
Narrowed REGISTRY_REREAD_FAILED to fire only when the chain did not verify; bounded the chain read at 8s so it degrades to "not read" rather than consuming the route budget.
rejectedApproaches: Widen the `confirmed` substring heuristic with a fourth word — the error it risks is the worse one (declaring a registration confirmed that is not). A canary now asserts the line verbatim and that it contains exactly three `includes(` calls.
Default `agentIdentifier` from the tokenId — forbidden by the operator ruling of 2026-07-31; it stays null and the response says so.
Keep the wallet-keyed registry lookup as a fallback beside the decode — a source that can answer confidently and wrongly is worse than an honest refusal.
